trust_decision.summary: The `id` field in an imported archive's agent.yml is trusted to name the registry directory, which is then removed if it exists and recreated (agents_dir / id); the fix ignores the archive id, assigns a fresh UUID and reserves the directory with an exclusive mkdir. The same commit also confines the edit route's server-side file read to the agent workspace.

landing_point.why: The summary names agent profile import. AgentRegistry.import_agent is the only importer, and it reads agent_data["id"] and joins it to agents_dir before calling rmtree.

It is fixed only because it shares import_agent, so this is a WHERE-type site. The edit-route read fix at local_operator/server/routes/chat.py:644-654 is a separate protection in another module.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue that a valid-looking archive UUID should be kept so export/import round-trips restore the same identity (old tests asserted imported.id == original id at tests/unit/test_agents.py:1663 per fix.diff:891). That reading leaves a repeated import that overwrites an existing local agent's private history.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The profile name must be kept verbatim even when it looks like a path ('../Display name is not a path'), and permitted instruction files (system_prompt.md) must still copy. Export->import round trips and old-version profiles must still import, while the original agent stays intact. On the edit side, workspace-relative and absolute in-workspace paths, in-workspace symlinks, a filesystem-root workspace, and caller-supplied buffers (including "") must keep working.

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The data only exists if an earlier vulnerable import wrote it, and after the fix no remote route sets an id (AgentEditFields has no id, local_operator/agents.py:170-175)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: migrate_legacy_agents builds agents_dir / id from agents.json ids; a planted import-from-legacy-bundle route could feed archive ids here
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A legacy migration path that trusts stored ids is plausible, and a maintainer would see it as local-only data.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a clone/duplicate-from-archive variant that keeps the source id or writes to agents_dir / supplied id
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Clone already copies a whole agent directory; a 'restore from backup' variant that keeps identity is a natural feature request.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a hub pull that extracts the downloaded archive with its own loop instead of calling import_agent (a second implementation in local_operator/clients/radient)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The hub client downloads to a path built from agent_id; a direct extraction would be a realistic optimisation, at distance from agents.py.

O9_family: CWE-22 path traversal from an untrusted archive metadata field into a directory path, with destructive rmtree/overwrite of an existing destination. The same commit also fixes an unconfined server-side file read on the edit route.

O10_build.project_tests: tests/unit/test_agents.py (import/export roundtrip ~1640-1670), tests/unit/server/test_server_agent_import_export.py; the fix adds tests/unit/test_agent_import_boundary.py and tests/unit/server/test_edit_workspace_boundary.py

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Sanitise or regex-check the archive id (basename or UUID format) but keep it, leaving 'if exists: rmtree' so a repeated or colliding valid UUID still destroys an existing agent.
